Table Description:
The AllApplications table contains all (building, layout permission, etc) applications in the BuildNow system, regardless of their current status. This includes draft applications still being prepared by citizens or architects, applications under various stages of review by government authorities (DTCP, GHMC, HMDA), failed applications requiring corrections, and completed applications (approved/rejected)...

This table stores both submitted and non-submitted applications. Submitted applications are separately maintained in the SubmittedApplications table. To identify draft or non-submitted applications, exclude records that exist in the SubmittedApplications table.

Official file reference number assigned to each application. Also called file number (file no.). It will be generally used as a key to search application details by citizen / officer / architect....
Date and time when the application record was first created in the system. Use for temporal analysis, filtering by creation periods, or tracking application created patterns.
This is the main classification for the type of application proposed.
Specific subcategory within the application_type that details the exact nature of the construction/development work. Provides more granular classification than application_type.

Table Description: The ApplicationOfficers table tracks individual officer assignments and processing activities for each submitted application. This table maintains a detailed log of which officers are assigned to specific applications, their processing timelines, and SLA compliance. Each record represents a single officer's involvement in an application's review process, capturing both assignment and completion timestamps.

fields.field_description: Unique identifier for each officer assignment record
Foreign key linking to the specific application in SubmittedApplications table. Identifies which application this officer assignment relates to.
Foreign key referencing the specific officer assigned to this application. Links to Officers table for officer details and contact information.
Specific role classification of the assigned officer within the processing hierarchy

Time remaining (in seconds) for this officer to complete their assigned verification task within SLA guidelines. Used for deadline monitoring and escalation triggers

SLA Breached (Exceed): remaining_time_left_in_sec < 0
At-Risk: remaining_time_left_in_sec <= 172800
SLA Within: remaining_time_left_in_sec >= 0 (included atrisk applications)
SLA Within: remaining_time_left_in_sec > 172800 (not included atrisk applications)

we are using this field is calcualte the Total Pending Days: Ceil((sla_time_in_sec - remaining_time_left_in_sec)/86400)
Date and time when this specific officer was assigned to review this application. Marks the start of this officer's processing timeline.
Date and time when the officer completed their assigned verification task. Used for calculating individual processing times and efficiency metrics.

Total time allocated (in seconds) for this officer's specific verification task as per Service Level Agreement. Used for SLA compliance monitoring and performance evaluation.

we are using this field is calcualte the Total Pending Days: Ceil((sla_time_in_sec - remaining_time_left_in_sec)/86400)

Table Description:
The ApplicationOfficersHierarchy table establishes the complete officer hierarchy structure for each submitted application. Unlike ApplicationOfficers which tracks individual assignments sequentially, this table provides a comprehensive view of all officers assigned across all levels (L1-L4) and specialized roles for a specific application.

This table serves as the master assignment matrix, showing the complete organizational structure responsible for processing each application.

fields.field_description: Primary key and foreign key linking to the specific application in SubmittedApplications table. Each application has exactly one hierarchy record defining its complete officer structure.
Officer ID assigned at Level 1 for processing the application.
Level 1 TVO ID assigned to the application.
Level 1 STO ID responsible for the application.
Level 1 ACP officer ID assigned to the application.
Level 1 APO/JPO ID assigned to the application.
Level 1 SI officer ID handling the application.
Level 1 TTVO ID associated with the application.
Officer ID at Level 2 responsible for further processing of the application.
Officer ID at Level 3 involved in reviewing or approving the application.
Officer ID at Level 4 for final-level application processing or decision-making.

Table Description: The Officers table maintains the master registry of all government officers involved in the TG-bPASS application processing workflow. This includes officers from various departments and authorities (DTCP, GHMC, HMDA) as well as line department officers (Revenue, Irrigation, Fire, Title verification) who participate in the multi-level verification process.

fields.field_description: Unique identifier for each officer. Primary key used to reference officers in application assignments, workflow tracking, and departmental verification processes.
Full name of the government officer. Used for identification, communication, and reporting purposes in the application processing workflow.
Official job title or position of the officer (e.g., Assistant City Planner, Planning Officer, Director, Commissioner, Tehsildar, Site Inspector).
Hierarchical level classification of the officer within the processing workflow (L1, L2, L3, L4 for primary processing officers, or specialized categories for line department officers).
Geographic or administrative zone assigned to the officer for territorial jurisdiction.

Table Description: It tracks multiple scrutiny attempts for each building plan application. It records whether each scrutiny run was successful or failed, along with timing and other data.

fields.field_description: Foreign key linking to the specific application in SubmittedApplications table. Establishes which application requires line department verification.
Timestamp when the workload detail record was created
Timestamp when the workload was completed
Current status of the workload (COMPLETED, IN_PROGRESS, CALLED_TO_AUTOCAD, FAILED)
Plot area measurement as documented in the application
Actual time taken for scrutiny process in seconds

Table Description: The ApplicationLineDepartmentDetails table tracks the review process by specialized line departments for submitted applications. Certain applications require additional approvals from specific government departments beyond the primary processing authority (DTCP/GHMC/HMDA). This table maintains records of officer assignments, processing timelines, and completion status for these departmental reviews.

fields.field_description: Unique identifier for each line department verification record. Primary key for tracking individual departmental review assignments.
Foreign key linking to the specific application in SubmittedApplications table. Establishes which application requires line department verification.
Foreign key referencing the specific officer assigned to review this application from the line department. Links to Officers table for officer details.

Department classification of the assigned officer (REVENUE for land verification, IRRIGATION for water clearances, TITLE for ownership verification, FIRE for safety clearances). Determines the type of verification required.
Time remaining (in seconds) for the officer to complete their departmental review within prescribed SLA timelines. Used for deadline monitoring and escalation alerts.
Date and time when the specific officer was assigned this application for departmental review. Marks the start of line department processing timeline.
Current status of the departmental verification process. "Yet to Verify" indicates pending review, "Completed" indicates finished verification by the assigned officer.
Date and time when the officer completed their departmental review and submitted their verification decision. Used for calculating processing time and efficiency metrics.
Total time allocated (in seconds) for this specific departmental verification as per Service Level Agreement. Used for SLA compliance monitoring and performance measurement.
